questions.question: What does godot-demo-projects do, and who runs it?
questions.answer: It collects independent Godot Engine demo projects. Each project.godot folder is an importable project; developers scan the repository in Godot project manager or obtain individual demos. Demos can run natively or as published browser exports.
requiredFacts: Developers import through Godot project manager

# Godot demo projects

Each folder containing a `project.godot` file is a demo project meant to
be used with [Godot Engine](https://godotengine.org), the open source
2D and 3D game engine.

## Importing demos

To import all demos at once in the project manager:

- Clone this repository or [download a ZIP archive](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/archive/master.zip).
  - If you've downloaded a ZIP archive, extract it somewhere.
- Open the Godot project manager and click the **Scan** button on the right.
- Choose the path to the folder containing all demos.
- All demos should now appear in the project manager.

Alternatively, you can download individual demos from the
[Asset Store](https://store.godotengine.org/publisher/godot-foundation/),
either from the website or within Godot's project manager.

## Try the demos in your browser

Most of the demos are exported to GitHub Pages. They can be viewed
[here](https://godotengine.github.io/godot-demo-projects/).

> [!NOTE]
>
> The performance of Godot in a browser is lower than natively on
> desktop or mobile. For the best performance, consider downloading

questions.question: Name the principal components and responsibilities, distinguishing the repository from Pong.
questions.answer: The repository collects independent demos, not one game. Selected Pong uses project.godot to load pong.tscn; the scene assembles ball, paddles and boundaries. ball.gd moves/resets; paddle.gd handles movement and collision direction; wall.gd resets; ceiling_floor.gd bounces.
requiredFacts: Ball moves/resets and paddle handles movement

const DEFAULT_SPEED = 100.0

var _speed := DEFAULT_SPEED
var direction := Vector2.LEFT

@onready var _initial_pos := position

func _process(delta: float) -> void:

	position += _speed * delta * direction

questions.question: Which languages, framework systems and project boundaries organize the repository and selected Pong demo?
questions.answer: project.godot folders define separate Godot projects. Selected Pong uses GDScript, a .tscn scene and Compatibility renderer; README points to a separate C# Pong variant under mono/pong. Engine compatibility varies by branch.
requiredFacts: GDScript and tscn for selected Pong

# Godot demo projects

Each folder containing a `project.godot` file is a demo project meant to
be used with [Godot Engine](https://godotengine.org), the open source
2D and 3D game engine.

## Godot versions

- The [`master`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects) branch is compatible with Godot's `master` development branch (next 4.x release).
- The [`3.x`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/3.x) branch is compatible with Godot's `3.x` development branch (next 3.x release).
- The other branches are compatible with the matching stable versions of Godot.
  - [Click here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/branches) to see all branches.
  - For example, the [`2.1`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/2.1)
    branch is for demos compatible with Godot 2.1.x.

# Pong with GDScript

A simple Pong game. This demo shows best practices
for game development in Godot, including
[signals](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/getting_started/step_by_step/signals.html).

Language: GDScript

Renderer: Compatibility

Check out this demo on the Asset Store: https://store.godotengine.org/asset/godot-foundation/pong-with-gdscript-demo/

> [!NOTE]
>
> There is a C# version available [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/mono/pong).

questions.question: Where does selected GDScript Pong execution begin?
questions.answer: project.godot sets run/main_scene to res://pong.tscn, whose script resources attach gameplay logic and whose signal connections route collisions. Godot drives lifecycle callbacks and Area2D signals, not a repository main function.

questions.answer: Scene resources bind paddle.gd, ball.gd, wall.gd and ceiling_floor.gd to matching Area2D nodes and connect area_entered to their handlers. This proves scene/resource dependencies and engine signal dispatch, not ordinary direct function-call edges.

# Pong with GDScript

A simple Pong game. This demo shows best practices
for game development in Godot, including
[signals](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/getting_started/step_by_step/signals.html).

Language: GDScript

Renderer: Compatibility

Check out this demo on the Asset Store: https://store.godotengine.org/asset/godot-foundation/pong-with-gdscript-demo/

> [!NOTE]
>
> There is a C# version available [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/mono/pong).

## How does it work?

The walls, paddle, and ball are all
[`Area2D`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_area2d.html)
nodes. When the ball touches the walls or the paddles,
they emit signals and modify the ball.

questions.question: Where does Z, paddle movement input, enter and get transformed?
questions.answer: project.godot defines left/right move-up/down actions. paddle.gd._ready derives action names from the lowercase node name; _process subtracts up strength from down, scales by MOVE_SPEED and delta and clamps y between 16 and viewport height minus 16.
